problem_text:
A logistics company must select packages to load onto a cargo plane. Available packages are:
* Package 1: volume 25 m³, revenue $296
* Package 2: volume 19 m³, revenue $106
* Package 3: volume 14 m³, revenue $45
* Package 4: volume 25 m³, revenue $116
* Package 5: volume 12 m³, revenue $108
* Package 6: volume 4 m³, revenue $182
* Package 7: volume 25 m³, revenue $42
* Package 8: volume 7 m³, revenue $290
* Package 9: volume 40 m³, revenue $33
* Package 10: volume 24 m³, revenue $88
* Package 11: volume 11 m³, revenue $193
* Package 12: volume 30 m³, revenue $222
* Package 13: volume 22 m³, revenue $163
* Package 14: volume 50 m³, revenue $158
* Package 15: volume 21 m³, revenue $228
* Package 16: volume 48 m³, revenue $97
* Package 17: volume 29 m³, revenue $80
* Package 18: volume 43 m³, revenue $247
* Package 19: volume 9 m³, revenue $219
* Package 20: volume 35 m³, revenue $190
* Package 21: volume 21 m³, revenue $72
* Package 22: volume 2 m³, revenue $84
* Package 23: volume 45 m³, revenue $192
* Package 24: volume 21 m³, revenue $114
* Package 25: volume 8 m³, revenue $158

The aircraft's cargo hold has a maximum capacity of 413 m³. Choose the package combination that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this volume constraint. Each package is either fully loaded or left behind.
